subject: Green Line Transit Area Permit Parking Zone
overview: City officials presented a pilot program to consolidate street-by-street permit parking into a single district-wide zone near the Green Line Extension stations. The meeting addressed resident concerns regarding parking congestion, enforcement technology, and neighborhood infrastructure before a scheduled Traffic Commission vote.

items.title: Program Overview and Map
items.summary: Officials introduced the Green Line Transit Area Permit Parking Zone, a pilot program designed to allow residents within the designated zone to park on any included street rather than being restricted to their own.

items.title: Timeline and Regulatory Background
items.summary: The proposal follows recommendations from a 2020 advisory commission and is scheduled for a formal hearing and vote by the Traffic Commission on April 9, 2024.

items.title: Proposed Operational Changes and Pilot Mechanics
items.summary: While the zone consolidation would allow more flexibility for residents, the city confirmed that visitor pass systems, enforcement hours, and license plate scanning technology will remain unchanged.

items.title: Public Feedback: Parking Influx and Safety Concerns
items.summary: Residents expressed concern that the district-wide model could lead to overcrowding on dead-end streets and questioned how the change would impact snow plowing and winter emergency operations.

items.title: Transit Infrastructure and Pedestrian Safety
items.summary: Discussion expanded to address the perceived lack of adequate sidewalks and bicycle lanes near the new transit stations, leading to a review of planned capital improvements and the city's Complete Streets policy.

items.title: Next Steps and Data Collection
items.summary: The city will utilize SeeClickFix for data collection during the pilot and plans to re-evaluate the program's success based on resident feedback after implementation.
